title: APIs
description: REST, gRPC, contracts, OpenAPI, CRUD, serialization, versioning, pagination, filtering, sorting, and idempotency.

lessons.title: REST and API Contracts
lessons.summary: REST exposes resources through URLs and standard HTTP methods; contracts let teams work independently.
lessons.explanation: REST exposes resources through URLs and standard HTTP methods; contracts let teams work independently. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: GET /users and POST /users describe resource actions clearly.
interview_questions: When would you apply rest and api contracts?
What failure mode appears when rest and api contracts is misunderstood?

lessons.title: OpenAPI, Swagger, and CRUD
lessons.summary: OpenAPI specifies endpoints; Swagger is an interactive UI. CRUD maps to POST, GET, PUT/PATCH, and DELETE.
lessons.explanation: OpenAPI specifies endpoints; Swagger is an interactive UI. CRUD maps to POST, GET, PUT/PATCH, and DELETE. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: FastAPI exposes Swagger at /docs from its OpenAPI schema.
interview_questions: When would you apply openapi, swagger, and crud?

lessons.title: Serialization and Versioning
lessons.summary: Serialization converts objects to JSON; deserialization converts JSON to objects. Versioning protects existing clients.
lessons.explanation: Serialization converts objects to JSON; deserialization converts JSON to objects. Versioning protects existing clients. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: /v2/users can introduce a breaking response shape without breaking /v1/users.
interview_questions: When would you apply serialization and versioning?
What failure mode appears when serialization and versioning is misunderstood?

lessons.title: Pagination and Idempotency
lessons.summary: Offset is simple; cursor is stable for large changing datasets. Idempotency makes retries safer.
lessons.explanation: Offset is simple; cursor is stable for large changing datasets. Idempotency makes retries safer. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: Retrying DELETE /users/5 is safe; retrying POST /users may duplicate data.
interview_questions: When would you apply pagination and idempotency?
What failure mode appears when pagination and idempotency is misunderstood?

coding_challenges.title: APIs status classifier
coding_challenges.instructions: Implement classify_status_code(code: int) -> str. Return success for 200-299, redirect for 300-399, client_error for 400-499, server_error for 500-599, and unknown otherwise.
coding_challenges.explanation: The challenge reinforces deterministic branching, status-code categories, and local test execution.
